subject: Post-demo: network & control-plane tradeoffs for on-prem inference
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finserve.co>, Mike Dalton <mike.dalton@cloudx.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 15:03:00 -0500
Subject: Post-demo: network & control-plane tradeoffs for on-prem inference

Thanks again for carving out time today — appreciated the thoughtful questions. Short recap and proposed next actions from our side: 

What we covered
- Demo recap: private deployment with customer-managed control plane (controller in customer's VPC) + on-prem inference workers. Showed live inference on a trimmed model and prefix-caching behavior.
- Tradeoffs: outbound control-plane vs air-gapped control plane, expected latency/throughput uplift with local workers, and KMS integration options.

Key asks from FinServe (Priya)
- Confirm whether control plane can be entirely isolated (no outbound internet)
- Network requirements and firewall rules for agents/heartbeats
- Proof points for encryption in transit + HSM/KMS support

Proposed immediate next steps (we can start these in parallel)
1) Small technical test (2–3 days): deploy a control plane inside your VPC with our agents in an on-prem lab that blocks outbound 0.0.0.0/0 but allows specific egress to the control plane. Measure connections, TLS handshakes, and KV cache behavior.
2) Air-gap feasibility spike (5–7 days): scope a variant where the control plane is an on-prem component paired over an internal network link (no public egress). We'll validate model updates and rollout mechanics.
3) Security evidence pack: we will collect KMS/HSM integration notes, mutual TLS diagram, and SOC2 artifacts relevant to this deployment.

Attachments: demo-traces.pdf (latency traces), network-constraints.xlsx (example firewall rule set).

Please confirm the two contacts for networking and procurement so we can request access for the test harness.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0128

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finserve.co>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Mike Dalton <mike.dalton@cloudx.com>, procurement@finserve.co
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 16:18:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: network & control-plane tradeoffs for on-prem inference

Ben — great summary, thank you. A few clarifying items from our infra/security teams: 

1) Air-gapped / no-outbound scenario: by "no outbound internet" we mean our appliances cannot make any connections to the public internet. We can open specific IP:port pairs to your control plane if needed, but we want to avoid TLS handshakes to public hostnames. Is it possible to run the control plane in our VPC behind a NAT with static egress IPs?

2) Heartbeats: what ports/protocols do agents use for heartbeats and control messages? We need a short list for firewall rules; our change window is next Tuesday.

3) HSM/KMS: we will require an HSM-backed key for model keys — do you have a flow for customers to use an external KMS (Bring Your Own Key)?

4) Can you run an initial latency test with the control plane in our us-east-1 VPC while agents are in our on-prem lab (no outbound DNS allowed)? We can provide a diagram — attaching current network topology.

Also looping in procurement — we'll need a mutual NDA and a standard SOW template for a POC.

Priya
Director, Platform Engineering | FinServe Inc
priya.shah@finserve.co

Folks — forwarding Priya's questions (below). Can you confirm feasibility and a realistic timeline for the two spikes she asked about:

- Latency test: control plane in FinServe's us-east-1 VPC + on-prem agents with blocked outbound DNS. We should capture TLS negotiation logs, connection counts, and token refresh behavior. Target: quick 2–3 day smoke test.
- Air-gap feasibility: what's required to operate without any public egress? Is there a supported pattern where the control plane and management APIs are fully on-prem? Rough estimate: 5–7 days for a focused spike, incl. test scripts.

Extras to advise on: exact ports/protocols, whether we can use static egress IPs (if required), and guidance on BYOK/HSM integration for model keys. 

Attachments: finserve-network-diagram.png (attached by Priya).

Can you scope a test plan and items we need from the customer (f/w ACLs, jump host access, cert exchange)? I will put together the ask to procurement for the NDA + SOW.

Thanks — Ben

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finserve.co>
Date: Fri, 19 Feb 2027 08:14:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-demo: network & control-plane tradeoffs for on-prem inference — FinServe asks

Ben / Lauren / Priya — quick technical plan below. We can start the smoke tests as soon as we have the following from FinServe: a) a small on-prem lab host reachable from their internal network, b) static egress IPs for the control plane (or a reachable private IP if we place control plane into their VPC), c) a test client cert for mTLS.

Proposed smoke test (48–72h)
- Step 0: exchange certificate material (customer provides client cert and CA chain).
- Step 1: deploy a control-plane instance in customer's us-east-1 account into a private subnet (no public IP). We will expose it on internal ALB with a fixed private IP behind NAT gateway or via an internal NLB — whichever FinServe prefers.
- Step 2: configure on-prem agent to only allow outbound to the control-plane private endpoint (no DNS to public internet). We will collect tcpdump during initial handshake and TLS session establishment.
- Step 3: run 500 request batch to measure cold-start and steady-state latency; capture KV cache hit rate.
- Step 4: validate key management: test a sample model key rotate using customer's BYOK flow pointing to their KMS (we will exercise HSM-backed key path if they provide credentials).

Deliverables
- runbook-test-plan.md (I will produce)
- tls-handshake-logs.tar.gz (snippets)
- latency-summary.csv

Constraints & notes
- If true air-gap (no egress of any kind) is required, we will need to run both control-plane and the management UI behind their internal network with a manual artifact sync flow for model updates. That increases complexity and will likely require a 7–10 day effort to validate rollout automation.

I'll draft the runbook and a minimal CF/Terraform patch to spin the control-plane node. If the customer prefers absolute no-egress, we should have an on-site engineer to perform model bundle uploads and sanity checks.

-- Aditya
Principal Systems Engineer | Redwood Inference
